messages.content: What is the acceleration a ball will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with a velocity of 5 m/s?

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The acceleration of a freely‑falling object near the Earth’s surface is essentially constant and equal to the acceleration due to gravity, \(g \approx 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\).  
When you throw a ball straight upward, it immediately begins to accelerate **downward** at this rate (the negative sign indicates direction opposite to the initial velocity). So the ball’s acceleration is

\[
a = -\,9.8\ \text{m/s}^2
\]

(negative because it points toward the Earth).  

If you were interested in how high the ball would rise, you could use the function `calculate_maximum_height` with an initial velocity of 5 m/s and the default gravity of 9.8 m/s².
